transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please come in and have a seat. What has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

I keep getting these really intrusive memories and images about something bad that happened, and they just pop into my head even when I’m trying not to think about it. I’m also having a lot of nightmares about it, and sometimes it feels like I’m right back there again.

Did these intrusive memories and nightmares start clearly after a specific traumatic event, and overall would you say your main problem is reliving that event or feeling generally low, hopeless, and down about everything most of the time?

Yeah, they definitely started after this one really bad thing that happened about a year ago. The main problem is reliving it over and over again, with the memories and nightmares, rather than just feeling generally low all the time.
Have these intrusive memories and nightmares been happening regularly for at least a month after the traumatic event, and are they still ongoing now?

Yeah, they’ve been happening pretty regularly ever since it happened, definitely more than a month after. They’re still going on now—most nights I have some kind of bad dream, and the memories pop up a few times a week at least.

Outside of the memories and nightmares, do you find yourself constantly on edge, easily startled, or going out of your way to avoid reminders of what happened, or is it more that your mood and energy have been generally low and flat most of the time?

It’s more the being on edge and avoiding things than just feeling flat. I’m always kind of tense and scanning around, checking exits and stuff, and I go out of my way to avoid certain places and situations that remind me of what happened.

How much are these symptoms interfering with your day-to-day life—for example, your ability to work, study, or maintain relationships—and have they been causing you significant distress for most of this past year?

They’re messing things up quite a bit—I have trouble concentrating at work and I’ve missed days because I’m exhausted from the nightmares or anxious about running into reminders. I’ve pulled back from friends and had more arguments at home because I’m so on edge, and it’s been like this pretty much the whole year.

When you have these memories or feel like you’re back in the situation, do you ever actually hear or see things that aren’t really there, or believe things that other people say don’t make sense or aren’t true outside the context of that trauma memory?

When it happens, it’s more like the memory takes over and I feel like I’m back there, and I kind of lose track of where I am for a bit, but I don’t see or hear completely new things that aren’t connected to what happened. I don’t really have strange beliefs outside of that—I know, logically, I’m here and it’s over, even though in those moments it doesn’t feel that way.

Since this event, have you noticed feeling persistently numb, detached, or unable to feel positive emotions, or having strong guilt or negative beliefs about yourself or the world because of what happened?

Yeah, I’ve had a lot more negative thoughts since it happened—I keep thinking there’s something wrong with me, like I’m weak or damaged for not getting over it. I also find myself thinking people aren’t really safe or trustworthy anymore, and sometimes I feel like the world is just a dangerous place and it’s partly my fault for not preventing what happened.
Since the trauma, have you been having problems like trouble falling or staying asleep, being unusually irritable or angry, or having difficulty concentrating because you feel constantly on guard?

Yeah, my sleep is pretty bad—I wake up a lot and it’s hard to fall back asleep. I’m on edge most of the time, get irritated and snap at people over small things, and my concentration is worse because I’m always kind of watching for something to go wrong.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please come in and have a seat. What has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports exposure to a severe traumatic event about one year ago, followed by persistent re-experiencing (intrusive memories, frequent nightmares, feeling as if back in the event), avoidance of trauma reminders, persistent negative beliefs about self and the world, hyperarousal (hypervigilance, sleep disturbance, irritability, concentration problems), and clear functional impairment for nearly a year. Symptoms began after the trauma, have lasted well beyond one month, and there is no evidence of primary psychotic or mood disorder dominating the picture. This presentation is most consistent with Post-traumatic stress disorder (F43.1).
